reader.requirement: At --std 85, when an indexed-file DELETE, READ, REWRITE, START or WRITE meets an invalid key condition, the file connector's I-O status (and the FILE STATUS item) must hold the 2x value before the INVALID KEY imperative or any USE procedure runs. This applies with and without the phrase and in every access mode. The witness covers dynamic access with the phrase on all five verbs; it does not cover random access, the statement with no phrase, or a nested I-O statement in the imperative.
reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectBehavior|DialectLevel in SequentialIoEmitter.cs: the one hit (line 593, SelectWhenOnlyForFilePhraseStatements) is the WHEN-phrase selector, not on this path. KeyedIoEmitter.cs, EcEmitter.cs and the DispatchEmitter __IoCheck body have none. The status assignment in FileConnector.Status has none.

reader.notes: The keyed verbs capture the runtime status into a local, store the FILE STATUS item, and run the USE hook before EmitInvalid renders the phrase branch, so action (1) comes before (2) and (3) on every path. No edition is consulted, and 1985's order is the later editions' order.

ON I-O in the outer program fired from a nested program's WRITE on a GLOBAL file.
